tools.name: list_skills
tools.description: List the available task skills with their source and content hash. User skills are disabled until the user explicitly enables them in pyRevit configuration.

tools.name: get_skill
tools.description: Read a skill: task guidance for Revit scripting. Read revit-scripting before your first script, then the skill for your task. Use list_skills for source and hash metadata. Skills: revit-scripting: Core Revit API scripting rules for the pyRevit agent runtime. Read before every query, dry run, or model change.; drawings: Use when producing drawings, sheets with title blocks, views and schedules on sheets, tags, dimensions, text and PDF export, e.g. "set up sheets", "tag all doors", "export to PDF".; extension-authoring: Use when turning a script into a pyRevit button or extension, bundle layout, bundle.yaml, search paths, reload and load check, e.g. "make this a button", "add a tool to the ribbon", "remove that tab".; family-editing: Use when editing Revit families, opening from the project, parameters, types, formulas and loading back, e.g. "add a parameter to these families", "create door types", "fix family formulas".; family-geometry: Use when building geometry inside families, reference planes, labelled dimensions, locked extrusions, formulas, shared parameters, nesting, e.g. "build a parametric family". Read family-editing first.; modeling: Use when building or changing model geometry, levels, walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, doors, windows, columns and rooms, e.g. "model this house", "add walls", "put windows in".; pyrevit-library: Use before writing raw Revit API code, map of the pyrevitlib (pyrevit.revit) and rpw helpers for lookups, element and view creation, parameters, units, transactions and navigation.; revit-files: Use when working with Revit files, .rvt, .rte, .rfa, .rft, templates and libraries, opening documents, save, print and export limits in guarded runs, e.g. "open this model", "find the mechanical template".; scheduling: Use when creating or reading schedules and quantities, fields, filters, sorting, grouping, placing on sheets and export, e.g. "make a door schedule", "count windows by type".; views: Use when creating, framing or navigating views, 3D views, sections, elevations, section boxes, crops, view templates, opening, zooming and pictures, e.g. "make a 3D view", "cut a section", "open the level 2 plan".

file.description: Another markdown file in the skill folder, as listed at the end of the skill (default SKILL.md).

tools.name: list_revit_instances
tools.description: List running Revit sessions that have the pyRevit agent host, with their version and process id. 'busy': true means that Revit is serving another call, from this session or another client, so it could not be pinged.

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Snapshot of the target Revit: versions, engines, agent policy, open document, active view, selection and levels. Call this first.

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: inspect_elements
tools.description: Describe elements by id: class, category, name, type, level, location, bounding box and (by default) every parameter with display and raw values.

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: lookup_pyrevit_api
tools.description: Search pyrevitlib (pyrevit.revit: query, create, update, units, ui, Transaction) and rpw (rpw.db) before writing raw Revit API code. Pass a module ('pyrevit.revit.db.create') to list its functions, a function name ('find_type', 'pyrevit.revit.db.create.create_gable_roof') for its signature and docstring, or words ('section box', 'room') to search. Works without Revit.

query.description: Module, function or class name, or search words.

tools.name: list_automation
tools.description: List the reviewed pyRevit and rpw automation APIs by stable identifier. An entry with invocable true runs through run_automation, taking the inputs it lists (element = an element id). Results are paginated and work without Revit.

tools.name: run_automation
tools.description: Run a reviewed read-only automation operation (invocable in list_automation) with the inputs it lists. Runs as a query, so model changes are rolled back. This does not accept Python source, module names or callable names.

id.description: Invocable automation identifier, such as pyrevit.units.parse-length.

engine.description: Script engine. Defaults to get_context.scripting.default_engine; see scripting.engines for each engine's Python version and syntax limits.

timeout_s.description: Seconds the script may run before it is stopped and rolled back with error 'timeout' (default 300, max 3600). Stops Python code, not a single long Revit API call. Not enforced when get_context shows agent.reckless: true; then a script that never ends hangs Revit.

document.description: Title or path of the document the run is meant for, as returned by get_context. If the active document differs, the run is refused with document_changed before anything runs. Pass the path when two open documents may share a title; a value containing a path separator is compared with the active document's path only, anything else with its title only.

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: lookup_revit_api
tools.description: Look up a Revit API type or member in the running Revit version, e.g. 'Wall', 'Autodesk.Revit.DB.Wall', 'Wall.Create', 'ElementId.Value'. Returns signatures, enum values and obsolete markers. Pass it as name, or as query like lookup_pyrevit_api.

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: show_elements
tools.description: Show elements to the user in the active view, without an approval prompt and without changing model elements: select them, temporarily isolate or hide them (Revit's temporary hide/isolate), or reset that mode. Target element ids and/or whole categories (resolved to the elements visible in the active view). When zoom fails, the response has zoomed=false and a zoom_failed error with Revit's message.

action.description: select (default), isolate, hide, or reset (end temporary hide/isolate in the active view).

categories.description: BuiltInCategory names such as OST_Windows or OST_Doors.

zoom.description: Also zoom the view to the elements.

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: navigate_revit_link
tools.description: Navigate an element link returned by inspect_elements. The active Revit document must still match the link; stale links return an actionable error. This selects or temporarily presents elements only.

zoom.description: Zoom to the linked elements (default true).

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: capture_view
tools.description: Take a PNG of a Revit view to check your work visually. mode 'export' (default) renders the view through Revit and works for any view by name or id; a name shared by several views fails with view_ambiguous listing their ids; pass 'view_type' to narrow by type. mode 'viewport' renders an open view through Revit cropped to the region its window shows now: the user's zoom, pan and temporary isolate, without selection highlight, and unaffected by other windows. mode 'screen' captures the active view's window exactly as the user sees it, including selection and temporary isolate; it fails with view_not_active for any other view and with view_obscured when another application covers the view. view '3d' renders a temporary 3D view of model categories only, framed by a section box around the whole model or around 'elements', seen from 'direction' (never saved); give 'eye' and 'target' for a perspective camera instead, or 'section' for a temporary section, elevation or plan cut at a height. 'detail_level' and 'display_style' override the view's own for this capture only, also for named views. The image is also saved under %APPDATA%\pyRevit\agent\captures for the user.

view.description: 'active' (default), '3d', a view name, a sheet number, or a view id.

view_type.description: Optional Revit ViewType name such as FloorPlan, CeilingPlan, Section, ThreeD or DrawingSheet; keeps only views of that type when a name is shared. Not with view 'active' or '3d'.

width.description: Image width in pixels, 320-2400 (default 1280). Larger images cost more tokens.

direction.description: view '3d' only: where the viewer stands (default southeast, looking down at 35 degrees).

elements.description: view '3d' only: element ids to frame; default is the whole model. Ignored with 'eye' and 'target'.

detail_level.description: Detail level for this capture only (view '3d' default: medium; named views keep their own). Not for mode 'screen'.

display_style.description: Display style for this capture only (view '3d' default: shaded_edges; named views keep their own). Not for mode 'screen'.

eye.description: view '3d' only: camera position in model coordinates, feet. Needs 'target'. Renders a perspective view with no section box.

target.description: view '3d' only: the point the camera looks at, feet. Needs 'eye'.

section.description: view '3d' only: a temporary section instead of the 3D views, framed on 'elements' or the whole model. 'normal' is the direction the view looks along: horizontal gives a section or elevation, [0,0,-1] a plan cut at origin z.

origin.description: A point on the cutting plane, feet.

normal.description: Look direction: horizontal, or [0,0,-1] for a plan.

depth.description: How far the view sees past the plane, feet. Default reaches the far side of the framed elements.

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: run_query
tools.description: Run a read-only Python script in Revit and return `result`, printed output, and any error with traceback. Model changes made during the run are rolled back and must not be made. A document the script creates, such as from `NewFamilyDocument` or `EditFamily`, is outside that rollback: it is reported in `changes.other_documents` with a `scope` instead of `rolled_back` and does not fail the run. A document opened from a file, such as with `OpenDocumentFile`, must not be modified: doing so fails the run with `other_document_modified`. The script itself runs with full access to Revit and the machine; the guard only covers what happens while it runs.

script.description: Python source. Assign `result` to return data.

title.description: Short label for the run record.

inputs.description: Values exposed to the script as the `inputs` dict.

engine.description: Script engine. Defaults to get_context.scripting.default_engine; see scripting.engines for each engine's Python version and syntax limits.

timeout_s.description: Seconds the script may run before it is stopped and rolled back with error 'timeout' (default 300, max 3600). Stops Python code, not a single long Revit API call. Not enforced when get_context shows agent.reckless: true; then a script that never ends hangs Revit.

workspace.description: Absolute path of a folder with your own helper modules (plan data, functions). It is on sys.path for the run and its modules are re-imported fresh every run, so `import house_plan` sees your latest edits.

document.description: Title or path of the document the run is meant for, as returned by get_context. If the active document differs, the run is refused with document_changed before anything runs. Pass the path when two open documents may share a title; a value containing a path separator is compared with the active document's path only, anything else with its title only.

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: run_modify
tools.description: Run a Python script that changes the model. With dry_run=true the change set is returned and everything is rolled back. Otherwise, under agent policy 'ask', Revit shows the user an approval prompt with the changed elements isolated; under policy 'auto' the change is committed directly. Kept changes become one undo entry named 'Agent: <title>'. Status 'rejected' means the user discarded the changes.

script.description: Python source. Open transactions with DB.Transaction; assign `result` to return data.

title.description: What the change does; shown to the user and used as the undo name.

dry_run.description: Preview only: run, report the change set, roll back.

inputs.description: Values exposed to the script as the `inputs` dict.

engine.description: Script engine. Defaults to get_context.scripting.default_engine; see scripting.engines for each engine's Python version and syntax limits.

timeout_s.description: Seconds the script may run before it is stopped and rolled back with error 'timeout' (default 300, max 3600). Stops Python code, not a single long Revit API call. Not enforced when get_context shows agent.reckless: true; then a script that never ends hangs Revit.

workspace.description: Absolute path of a folder with your own helper modules (plan data, functions). It is on sys.path for the run and its modules are re-imported fresh every run, so `import house_plan` sees your latest edits.

document.description: Title or path of the document the run is meant for, as returned by get_context. If the active document differs, the run is refused with document_changed before anything runs. Pass the path when two open documents may share a title; a value containing a path separator is compared with the active document's path only, anything else with its title only.

revit.description: Target Revit: a year (e.g. "2024"), a process id, or the name of the pyRevit clone the session runs. Leave it out unless list_revit_instances shows more than one session.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Read a recorded run by run_id, or by the request_id of a request that got no answer: response, script, and pages of a result too large to return inline (use offset/length).

offset.description: Character offset into a truncated result.

tools.name: get_recording
tools.description: Read a session recording the user made with 'pyrevit agent record start' and 'stop': a JSON timeline of element changes per transaction (category, family and type, location), pyRevit commands with their output, log messages and tracebacks, extension breadcrumbs from recorder.mark, view and selection changes, dialogs, warnings and screenshot file references. Without recording_id it lists recent recordings. Screenshots are files under the recording's directory; the events carry their relative path. A recording still in progress can be read too. Recording files are stored locally; recording data returned to the client may be sent to its model provider.

recording_id.description: Id from the recordings list or from 'record start'.

offset.description: Index of the first event to return (default 0).
